The sky over Krator · reference site Voth, 40° S

The Krator System

Krator is a tidally locked moon of an ice giant, one of seven bodies in a tight family. The giant hangs fixed in the north-east of every sky; six other moons ride the line of its rings. The figures follow the shared sky model in core/atmos/sky.

Orbits to scale

Distance from the giant

A 3D model you can turn: every moon at its real period, lit by the sun.
Drag to turn, scroll or pinch to zoom; double-click a moon to follow it close up, the giant or empty space to come back. The moons are drawn larger than life so they can be seen.

Distances are drawn to scale (one pixel is about 1,100 km); the bodies are not. Every moon orbits in the giant's equator, so from Krator they all travel along the ring line and pass behind the giant.

Day

Io-like volcanic

Torn by the giant's tides into constant eruption: dark lava flows, glowing vents on its night side, ash plumes over its limb. It crosses the giant's face once a day.

Vesta-like Trojan

A small, lumpy world sharing Krator's own orbit, 60° ahead: squashed and lopsided, grey and cratered, with a vast basin over its south pole. It hangs fixed beside the giant and waxes and wanes once a day.

The Station

Broken torus station

A dead ring station still circling Krator, far above its air: a sector torn out, a spoke snapped, and a long trail of wreckage spreading out behind it along its orbit. To the eye it is a small grey loop with a glittering tail, crossing the sky in minutes; a telescope shows the broken ring plainly. It goes dark when it passes into Krator's shadow.

The giant's neighbours

The star's planets

The giant, with Krator and its moons, goes round a Sun-like star once a year at 1 AU. Three planets circle inside its orbit and three outside. Names are working names; none is drawn in Krator's sky yet.

Ash

Dark cratered planet

The innermost: a Mars-sized ball of near-black rock, airless and saturated with craters, its dayside baking at about 200 °C. It never strays more than 19° from the sun, so Krator sees it only low in a bright twilight.

Rust

Superterrestrial desert

A super-Earth half again Earth's width, Mars-like on a larger scale: rust deserts, dry sea basins, canyons and dust storms under a thin, hot carbon-dioxide sky. Too close to the sun to keep its oceans, it lost them long ago. It is half of a double planet: it and Cinder, an Earth-sized partner, go round a point in empty space between them every fourteen days, 400,000 km apart.

Cinder

Rust's partner

Rust's twin in the double planet: an Earth-sized, airless world, greyer and redder than Mars, of iron-stained basalt and old craters, with nothing on it but dust. It and Rust are locked face to face, so each hangs fixed in the other's sky.

Veil

Cloud world, a garden below

Venus-like from outside, a world of unbroken pale cloud, but not so hot: under a deck that reflects most of the light, a warm, humid green twilight of forests and shallow seas in thick, breathable-looking air, like Tohul. It goes round the sun three times for every two of the giant's years, a resonance that keeps the two from ever meeting.

Crown

Jovian giant

The largest planet of the star: a Jupiter-like giant two and a half times Jupiter's mass, cream and ochre belts with a long-lived red storm, and moons of its own. Its pull shaped the inner system.

Wanderer

Eccentric small planet

A Mercury-sized rock on a long, tilted ellipse, swinging from 5.9 AU, inside Frost's orbit, out to 17.7 AU. Like Pluto with Neptune it goes round twice for every three of Frost's years, so the two never meet. Probably flung out by Crown early in the system's history.

Apparent sizes are as seen from Krator, nearest to farthest. Phase periods are as seen from Krator: the Week's 7 days name Jimjam's weekdays, the Thirteen's 13 number them, and the two are new together every 91 days on the Double Dark. Masses for the giant and Krator follow from Krator's 24-hour orbit and its gravity; the moon maps are the owner's.
